physical_harm: Ante mortem injuries caused by a hard and blunt substance
number_of_offences: Charged under Sections 302 and 201 IPC; convictions upheld for both
premeditation_planning: Court found compelling motive through marriage documents and property transfer declaration
motive: Compelling motive for murdering her and her two minor children through marriage documents and property transfer declaration
key_evidence_accepted: The bodies of the three deceased victims were exhumed after three to six weeks of their unnatural death, and the convict was a mason and civil-works contractor competent to dig a soak-pit and dispose of the bodies. The convict had executed documents indicative of his marriage to the deceased and her declaration to transfer her property to him, providing compelling motive.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of the witnesses, including the informant and his aunt, as reliable, noting that the convict's inconsistent explanations and evasive replies led to the reporting of the matter to the police. The court also found the deposition of PW-4 and PW-3 to be steadfast and credible.
investigation_status: Charge sheet filed, bodies exhumed from soak pit

appeal_history.supreme_court: Modified death sentence to 30 years of incarceration without remission

prosecution_argument: The deceased woman assigned the construction of her house to the appellant-convict. They developed intimacy, and the convict started living with her. The informant and his aunt were regular visitors, and on one visit, they learned that only the convict was seen in the house. The matter was reported to the police, leading to the discovery of the decomposed bodies of the deceased and her children from a soak pit.
defence_argument: The chain of circumstantial evidence remains incomplete. The prosecution failed to collect direct evidence implicating the convict. The deceased was not on cordial terms with her in-laws, and there was a possibility that her in-laws committed the crime to grab the property. No witness testified that the convict concealed the bodies, and the object of the fatal assault was not found.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that where an offence like murder is committed in secrecy inside the house, the initial burden to establish the case is on the prosecution, but the nature and amount of evidence required is comparatively lighter. The court also emphasized that the accused living with the deceased within the confines of the home must provide a cogent explanation for the crime.
precedent_relied_upon: Trimukh vs State 2006 (10) SCC 681; Raj Kumar vs State (2007) (1) SCC 433; State vs Jaggu 2008 (12) SCC 51; Sushil Kumar vs State of Punjab 2009 (10) SCC 434; Swamy Shraddananda vs State of Karnataka 2008 (13) SCC 767; Sangeet vs State of Haryana 2013 (2) SCC 452; Gurvail Singh vs State of Punjab 2013 (10) SCC 631; Swamy Shraddananda and State of UP vs Sanjay Kumar 2012 (8) SCC 537; Sahib Hussain alias Sahib Jan vs State of Rajasthan 2013 (9) SCC 778; Anil alias Antony vs State of Maharashtra 2014 (2) SCALE 54
sentencing_rationale: The action of the convict was extremely brutal, grotesque, diabolical, and revolting. Incarceration for a further period of 30 years, without remission, in addition to the sentence already undergone, would be appropriate punishment in the facts and circumstances of the case.
